title: Events that changed the network
question: How did new towers, the 3G switch-off, and the 2019-20 bushfires and 2022 floods change measured mobile performance?
answer: Only two events leave a clear trace in quarterly data: the 2022 floods and the Telstra/Optus 3G switch-off. New towers leave none that speed medians can see, and the bushfire comparison fails its own check.
method: Event study with region and quarter fixed effects: touched regions against untouched ones, quarter by quarter, relative to the quarter before the event. Bars are 95% intervals. A result is only believed if the two groups moved together before the event.

events.name: 2022 Northern Rivers floods
events.finding: In the flood quarter the seven Northern Rivers LGAs ran a third more speed tests than other northern regions. Two quarters later their median speed was 23% lower. Both were back on track within about a year.
events.caveat: Lismore, the worst-hit LGA, has only six regions and shows nothing on its own. A quarterly median cannot see the days-long outages themselves.

events.name: Telstra and Optus 3G switch-off
events.finding: Outside the cities, speeds rose 22% and 39% relative to the cities four and five quarters after the switch-off, with no gap beforehand.
events.caveat: Every region was switched off at once, so non-city regions are compared with cities on the untested assumption that 3G-only devices were commoner outside them. Part of the rise may be the slowest devices leaving the sample, and regional 4G/5G upgrades in 2025 would look the same.

events.name: New Mobile Black Spot towers
events.finding: No measurable change in speed or test counts within 5, 10 or 20 km of a new tower.
events.caveat: This says speed medians cannot see coverage, not that the towers fail. They are built where there was no signal; their users are new rather than faster. O5 measures coverage directly.
sites:
Barrier Creek Highway  - Barrier Highway
(Between Broken Hill and Little Topar Hotel)

events.name: 2019-20 bushfires
events.finding: Burnt regions were already moving away from the controls before the fire season, and changing what counts as burnt flips the sign of the result.
events.caveat: Nothing here measures what the fires did. Burnt areas are mostly forested ranges with few tests, and the outages lasted days.

limits: Quarterly medians cannot see outages that last days.
Few touched regions: 22 near towers, 31 burnt, 40 flooded.
Who runs tests changes with events, so a change in median speed is partly a change in who is measuring.

sources.name: NSW Fire Extent and Severity Mapping 2019-20
